The narrator went into that pantry/kitchen to prepare a meal and, in an ordinary, deliberate act of cooking, heated oil or fat in a pan on the stove. There was no real fire and nothing burnt or charred; nevertheless the heated oil gave off smoke. Because that smoke was produced in the pantry where the automatic smoke/fire alarm is located, the alarm was triggered and rang while the narrator was still in the room. No drill, prank, other person, wrong alarm type, or historical incident was involved—the smoke from routine cooking set off the hall's fire alarm.
